html:
The Betoy, or Betoi, were an Indigenous people of the plains of Casanare and Arauca in eastern Colombia, near the foothills of the Andes. Their language is extinct and is known mainly from Jesuit records.

Jesuit missionaries from the New Kingdom of Granada worked among them in the 1700s. The Jesuit José Gumilla lived among the Betoy and described them in his book on the Orinoco, published in 1741. After the Jesuits were expelled in 1767, the missions declined, and the Betoy merged into other groups. Their neighbours included the Achagua and the U'wa in Colombia.
